title: Intrinsic valuation consistency engine
one_liner: Keep cash flows, discount rates, growth, reinvestment, returns and terminal assumptions mathematically and economically consistent.

selection.atomic_user_problem: Build or audit an intrinsic valuation whose major components do not contradict one another.
selection.distinctive_value: Encodes claim, unit, growth/reinvestment, terminal, bridge and stop-condition checks that are commonly omitted in ad hoc valuation.

source_faithfulness.rationale: Core doctrine is directly supported at the cited chapter/line anchors; workflow routing and current-data requirements are explicitly operational synthesis.

executability.rationale: The card has explicit inputs, ordered actions, observable outputs and hard stop conditions.

incremental_utility.comparison: The package-level release evaluation does not provide per-card attribution; individual behavioral evidence for this reference-only card remains pending.

falsifiable_boundedness.rationale: Non-use cases and invalid-input conditions alter routing or force a stop.

repetition_or_novelty.rationale: The governing consistency principles recur across multiple chapters; specific formulas remain valuable even when stated once.

do_not_trigger: Asset that will never generate cash flows and has no contingent cash-flow right.

reading.paraphrase: Cash flow to equity is discounted at cost of equity; cash flow to the firm is discounted at cost of capital.
reading.note: Source-grounded doctrine; runtime current-data and workflow adaptations are analyst inferences.

reading.locator: Chapter 7 > Cash Flows and Risk-Free Rates: The Consistency Principle > TXT lines 4515-4544; Conclusion lines 5023-5026
reading.paraphrase: Risk-free rate must match cash-flow currency, nominal/real basis and duration.
reading.note: Source-grounded doctrine; runtime current-data and workflow adaptations are analyst inferences.

reading.locator: Chapter 10 > TXT lines 6813-6820; Reinvestment formula line 7547; Conclusion lines 7558-7565
reading.paraphrase: FCFF is after tax and reinvestment but before debt payments; FCFE is after debt payments.
reading.note: Source-grounded doctrine; runtime current-data and workflow adaptations are analyst inferences.

reading.locator: Chapter 11 > Fundamental Determinants of Growth > formulas TXT lines 7940, 7957, 8058, 8078
reading.paraphrase: Expected growth is linked to reinvestment and the return earned on that reinvestment, for equity and firm cash flows.
reading.note: Source-grounded doctrine; runtime current-data and workflow adaptations are analyst inferences.

reading.locator: Chapter 12 > Closure in Valuation > formulas TXT lines 8728, 8745, 8835-8845; Closing Thoughts lines 9126-9138
reading.paraphrase: Terminal value requires a coherent stable-growth state, survival assessment and reinvestment consistent with stable growth.
reading.note: Source-grounded doctrine; runtime current-data and workflow adaptations are analyst inferences.

reading.locator: Chapter 15 > Firm Valuation > formulas TXT lines 11301-11305; Chapter 34 lines 24354-24363
reading.paraphrase: Equity and firm approaches should reconcile when leverage, cash flows and discount rates are modeled consistently; unstable leverage favors firm/APV approaches.
reading.note: Source-grounded doctrine; runtime current-data and workflow adaptations are analyst inferences.

interpretation.model: Keep cash flows, discount rates, growth, reinvestment, returns and terminal assumptions mathematically and economically consistent.
decision_rules: Tie growth to reinvestment and returns.
Cross-check equity and firm approaches where feasible.
assumptions: Current company, market, accounting and regulatory facts are obtained at runtime from authoritative sources.
Book examples illustrate mechanics and are not current defaults.

future_scenarios.expected_use: Execute the steps, disclose assumptions, and stop rather than invent missing current inputs.

stop_conditions: Required current facts or market inputs cannot be sourced or bounded.
Cash-flow claim and discount rate cannot be made consistent.
Terminal or reverse-valuation system is mathematically invalid or underidentified.

out_of_scope: using a perpetual-growth denominator with r <= g
failure_modes: Using book case numbers or U.S. historical observations as current universal defaults.
Hiding uncertainty behind a precise point value.
Continuing after unresolved entity, period, currency, unit, formula or data-vintage mismatch.
limitations: The source is a 2025 valuation text; current accounting, tax, regulatory and market facts require separate verification.
Stage 0-1.6 validates evidence and contract design, not live-model investment performance.
ask_user_when: Valuation purpose, claim, date, currency or control/minority perspective would materially change the model.
Several plausible narratives produce materially different values and the user must choose a scenario policy.
escalate_when: A regulated fairness opinion, tax/legal conclusion or transaction execution is requested.
Complex derivatives, insolvency waterfall or jurisdiction-specific regulatory capital requires specialist review.
